title: 10 Grounding Techniques for Anxiety That Actually Work
description: Evidence-based grounding exercises to calm anxiety in the moment. Techniques for panic, dissociation, and overwhelming emotions.

content.text: When anxiety or panic hits, grounding techniques can bring you back to the present. Here are 10 that actually work, backed by clinical experience and research.
This activates the parasympathetic nervous system, directly counteracting fight-or-flight.
Cold activates the dive reflex, slowing heart rate and calming the nervous system:

items: Splash cold water on your face
Squeeze a stress ball or pillow

content.text: 'I notice I'm feeling anxious. My heart is racing. This is uncomfortable but not dangerous. This will pass.'
Give your anxious brain something else to do:

items: Recite song lyrics or a poem

content.text: Tense each muscle group for 5 seconds, then release:

items: Start with feet, move up to face
Notice the contrast between tension and relaxation

content.text: Picture a place where you feel completely safe. Engage all senses—what do you see, hear, smell, feel? Spend 2-3 minutes there.
Pick up an object and describe it in extreme detail:

items: How it feels in different parts of your hand

content.text: From DBT, for when emotions are overwhelming:

items: Intense exercise: 20-30 seconds of high intensity
Paced breathing: Exhale longer than inhale
Progressive relaxation: Tense and release muscles
Practice when calm so techniques are automatic when anxious
Have a few go-to techniques that work for you
The best technique is the one you'll actually use

content.text: Grounding techniques don't eliminate anxiety, but they can reduce its intensity and help you ride it out. The key is practice—make these automatic so they're available when you need them most.
